L6·N5866unmasked layer
This neuron fires on proper-name tokens—brand names, surnames, composers, product/company names—particularly the final sub-word piece of a multi-token name within comma-separated enumerations (e.g. Graph|Tech, God|un|ov, Med|itech, Can|ales), and is essentially inert on the BOS token/plain narrative text.

The neuron activates on tokens that are isolated or appear in parentheses, often numerical values or phrases (e.g. "to", "(name)").
text excerpts related to health, technology, interpersonal communication, and political issues with factual or report-like presentation styles.
L13·N4208unmasked layer
This neuron is broadly active on ordinary running prose and peaks at the comma (or coordinating "and") that separates items in a coordinated list/clause, while it drops to zero on rare, technical or word-fragment tokens (proper-noun parts, sub-word pieces like "operand-i", "v-ina", "pe-eling").

L24·N2131unmasked layer
This neuron fires on the highly predictable "glue" token that completes a fixed collocation or multiword unit — e.g. the *for* in "Named for", the *well* in "as well as", the *-point* in "3-point", the *irl* completing "Swirl" — i.e. it marks mid-phrase forced continuations rather than any single lexical item (the same kind of position, e.g. "bit *by* bit", "89*.*79", can strongly suppress it).
